label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The issue is that the `busy` state remains `true` after a failed export because the `exportReport` function's `.catch()` handler is missing. When the fetch fails (e.g., due to a server error), the `setBusy(false)` call in the `.then()` block never executes, leaving the button disabled. The fix should add error handling to reset `busy` to `false`.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in `ExportButton` only resets the `busy` state to `false` when the `exportReport` promise resolves successfully. If the export fails (e.g., due to a non-2xx HTTP response), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button indefinitely. To fix this, the `catch` block of the `exportReport` promise should also set `busy` to `false` to re-enable the button after a failure. This ensures the button is usable again without requiring a page reload.
